source.author: lucan
source.text: Tum vultu semper celante timorem, Intrepidus superum sedes et templa vetusti Numinis, antiquas Macetum testantia vires, Circuit: et, nulla captus dulcedine rerum, Non auro cultuque deum, non moenibus urbis, Effossum tumulis cupide descendit in antrum.
source.text_original: Tum vultu semper celante timorem, / Intrepidus superum sedes et templa vetusti / Numinis, antiquas Macetum testantia vires, / Circuit: et, nulla captus dulcedine rerum, / Non auro cultuque deum, non moenibus urbis, / Effossum tumulis cupide descendit in antrum.
source.text_english: Then, with a face that always concealed his fear, fearless, he went round the dwellings of the gods above and the temples of the ancient divinity, bearing witness to the old might of the Macedonians; and, with no attraction in the sights around him, not by the gold or adornment of the gods, not by the walls of the city, he eagerly descended into the cavern dug out from the tombs.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at Iuno Argolicas pariter Macetumque per urbes spargit inexpertos temptare parentibus austros Aesoniden; iam stare ratem remisque superbam poscere quos revehat rebusque in saecula tollat.
reuse.text_original: at Iuno Argolicas pariter Macetumque per urbes / spargit inexpertos temptare parentibus austros / Aesoniden; iam stare ratem remisque superbam / poscere quos revehat rebusque in saecula tollat.
reuse.text_english: But Juno, through the Argive cities and the cities of the Macedonians alike, spreads the word that Aeison’s son is to try winds untested by his father; already the ship stands and, proud of its oars, asks for those whom it may carry back and raise by its deeds to the ages.
